title: Nvidia's board reportedly moves to oust Jensen Huang — no heir named
summary: The Wall Street Journal reports Nvidia's board is preparing to remove Jensen Huang after a second reported affair, a House subpoena threat and a falling stock, with no succession plan in view. Then Anthropic's second amended IPO filing says it has met its own threshold for AI-accelerated research on what it expects rather than what it has observed, and Senator Josh Hawley's call for a nationwide data center pause set against new evidence on who actually raised power bills.

topics: Nvidia board reportedly preparing to oust Jensen Huang (WSJ via TechCrunch, 11 November 2026): board could meet as soon as Wednesday evening, no decision reported at gather time; stock ~-8% after hours, ~-11% over five days; NYT (five ex-employees) reports a second affair with Kimberly Powell, VP of health care and a direct report, unconfirmed, Huang 'I don't think you should be talking to me directly'; House chairmen Moolenaar/Mast/Crawford briefing request with end-of-Wednesday deadline and subpoena threat; Huang ~3.6% stake without voting control ('easier to dislodge', Ann Lipton); Lipton: 'You just can't lie about it under the federal securities laws'; Oct 29 statements ('not unusual or unexpected', 'completely normal') called false by Transformer's Shakeel Hashim; Henderson 'I would be furious if they didn't tell me'; The Information: $7.5B chip purchases via Shanghai Century Litong incl. banned chips; CSET (Hannas, Chang) 'not, by itself, evidence of stolen technology'; ~60 direct reports, no succession plan, outside search firm (Bloomberg); TechCrunch's 'highly unscientific' successor list (Kress, Buck). Unresolved on air: Ada says the direct-report affair moves the board; Alan says the subpoena.

Anthropic S-1/A Amendment No. 2 (10 November 2026): 'we made a determination that we have met this threshold based on what we expect from future models and our overall rate of progress, rather than on what we have observed from current models' under the RSP's 'observe or expect' AI R&D threshold (~two years of 2018-2024-rate progress in one, per Yahoo); wording walk from Oct 26 ('until after it has occurred') to Nov 2 ('may imminently meet') to Nov 10 (met); 'evaluating the implications', 'will release further reports'; 'considering updates to our Responsible Scaling Policy to keep humans in control'; 'do not anticipate being able to safely use Claude to fully autonomously design and build successive generations'; 'may lose visibility across certain processes'; models 'increasingly perform our research, including our safety research'; 'Our monitoring does not cover all of our internal and external deployments'; METR called August's below-threshold argument 'overstated', 'plausible' crossed by mid-July; Ray Wang 'deliberately overstated'; AI and 'super intelligence' used interchangeably. Ada: a forecast promoted to a finding; Alan: 'observe or expect' is the only tripwire that fires before you trip; both watching whether the promised policy update says who can stop a training run.

Hawley's nationwide data center moratorium call (11 November 2026): first Senate Republican per reporting; 'MORATORIUM on data centers' on a Senate GOP priority list; spokesperson: until 'a bill of rights giving taxpayers guarantees of no rate increases'; no bill, no duration; contrasted with Hawley-Blumenthal Guaranteeing Rate Insulation from Data Centers Act (own generation) and Sanders/Ocasio-Cortez moratorium (safety, workers, prices). Evidence: Wharton/HBS working paper (Netessine et al., via WaPo's Shannon Osaka) ~4% of residential rate increases 2020-2025, 15% industrial, PJM exception, EPRI doubling-with-4%-drop, Brattle's Hledik. Local: Boulder County 50 kW limit; Mississippi MDEQ notices to SpaceXAI ($25k/day). CoreWeave Q3: ~$9B prepayments expected, short-term >$40M/MW-year vs $20-25M on 4-5-year contracts. Alan: 'guarantee' is a slogan, own-generation is the buildable rule; Ada: the slogan prices permission.

dives.why_it_matters: Nvidia investors and export-control watchers care because a leadership change at the company whose chips set the pace of AI, made without a succession plan, lands in the middle of a congressional fight over chip rules.

dives.story: The line Anthropic says it crossed
dives.why_it_matters: Lab-oversight and RSP watchers care because this is the first time a frontier lab has formally declared its own AI-accelerated-research tripwire met, in a document carrying legal liability, and what that tripwire actually triggers is still undefined.

dives.story: A pause on the power bill
dives.why_it_matters: Anyone renting compute or planning data center capacity cares because a bipartisan national moratorium would reprice every already-built megawatt, while the rate evidence says the bill it promises to protect was mostly not driven by data centers.

lore.note: Alan holds that a moratorium conditioned on 'guarantees of no rate increases' is a slogan no utility can deliver, and that the only buildable version is making data centers bring their own generation; Ada answers that the slogan is the point — it prices permission. Unresolved.
